rics.description: Earnings, Hourly, Hourly compensation, nonfarm business
rics.meaning: Hourly compensation, nonfarm business sector. Includes wages + benefits.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with productivity to compute unit labor costs (= compensation / productivity). Rising hourly comp without productivity gains = inflationary.

rics.description: Earnings, Hourly, Real hourly compensation, business, nonfarm
rics.meaning: REAL hourly compensation, nonfarm business — inflation-adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: True purchasing-power gauge. Stagnant for decades; recent surge largely deflation rather than nominal growth.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment Benefits QQ - Acutal, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Employment benefits cost change QoQ.
rics.how_to_use: Benefits inflation (mostly health insurance, retirement) is stickier than wages.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment Wages QQ, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Employment wages QoQ change.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner wage signal than aggregate compensation. Pair with ECI total.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, benefit costs
rics.meaning: Employment Cost Index, benefit costs component.
rics.how_to_use: Health insurance + retirement contributions. Not as sticky as wage component but harder to reduce.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, total compensation
rics.meaning: Employment Cost Index, total compensation — wages + benefits.
rics.how_to_use: Fed's preferred wage gauge: includes benefits, controls for industry/occupation mix. Quarterly. >4% YoY is too high for 2% inflation target.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, total compensation, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: ECI total compensation QoQ change.
rics.how_to_use: Most market-relevant ECI series. Released on Fed black-out weeks; cleanest wage signal.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, total compensation, private ind, service-producing
rics.meaning: Employment Cost Index, total compensation (alternate framing) — companion series to aUSEMPCI/A. Quarterly BLS release.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aUSEMPCI/A. ECI is the Fed's preferred wage-pressure gauge over AHE because it controls for compositional shifts. Released Tue of NFP week — Fed pays close attention.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, wages and salaries
rics.meaning: ECI wages and salaries — strips out benefits.
rics.how_to_use: Pure wage gauge. AHE (in employment_hours) is monthly/noisier; ECI is quarterly/cleaner.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, wages and salaries, private industry
rics.meaning: ECI wages and salaries, private industry.
rics.how_to_use: Strip out government wages (which lag and are policy-driven).

rics.description: Labour Cost, Total-prelim
rics.meaning: Total labor costs — preliminary release.
rics.how_to_use: Watch the revisions; preliminary often gets revised meaningfully.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Unit, business
rics.meaning: Unit Labor Costs, business sector. ULC = compensation / productivity.
rics.how_to_use: Most useful labor-cost-driven inflation signal. ULC growth > productivity growth = wage-push inflation. Watch the 4-quarter change.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Unit, business, index
rics.meaning: Unit labor costs, business sector (index form) — labor cost per unit of output. Productivity-adjusted wage measure.
rics.how_to_use: ULC = compensation per hour ÷ output per hour. Sustained ULC growth above ~2% inconsistent with 2% inflation absent productivity gains. The Fed's go-to wage-inflation gauge alongside ECI.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Unit, business, nonfarm
rics.meaning: Unit labor cost growth, business nonfarm — pace of unit-labor-cost change. Productivity-adjusted wage-pressure indicator.
rics.how_to_use: Annualized growth rate. Above 4% sustained = wage-driven inflation pressure; below 2% = wage costs not inflationary. The Fed cites this in monetary-policy decisions.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Unit, business, nonfarm
rics.meaning: Unit Labor Costs, nonfarm business.
rics.how_to_use: Cleanest ULC measure (nonfarm strips out volatile farm sector). The Fed inflation hawks watch this directly.

rics.description: Labour Cost, Unit, business, nonfarm, index
rics.meaning: Unit labor costs, business nonfarm sector (index form) — same as aUSULCNF/A but in standardized index format for international comparison.
rics.how_to_use: Cleanest international-comparison ULC measure. Use for cross-country competitiveness analysis. Domestic analysts use aUSULCNF/A.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Hours of all persons, business, nonfarm
rics.meaning: Hours of all persons, nonfarm business — total hours worked.
rics.how_to_use: Denominator for productivity. Pair with output for productivity computation.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, business, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor
rics.meaning: Output per hour, business sector — productivity.
rics.how_to_use: Headline productivity gauge. Trend ~1.5%/yr; 2010s averaged below trend; AI may lift trend forward.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, business, Volume Index, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor
rics.meaning: Output per hour of all persons, business sector — broad productivity gauge. The headline productivity number cited in BLS releases.
rics.how_to_use: Trend ~1.5%/year; 2010s averaged sub-trend; 2024-25 showing recovery toward 2%. Most economically meaningful productivity measure. Trend matters more than quarterly: smooth with 4Q averages.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, business, index
rics.meaning: Output per hour of all persons, business sector, QoQ change — quarterly productivity-growth pace.
rics.how_to_use: Highly volatile quarterly. Smooth with 4Q averages for trend. The Fed cares about trend productivity for its implications for wage-inflation tolerance: high productivity allows higher wage growth without inflation.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, manufacturing
rics.meaning: Output per hour, manufacturing.
rics.how_to_use: Manufacturing productivity has historically grown faster than services. Slowed materially since 2010.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, nonfarm business
rics.meaning: Output per hour, nonfarm business — preliminary.
rics.how_to_use: Watch the revisions.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, nonfarm business
rics.meaning: Output per hour, nonfarm business.
rics.how_to_use: Strips out volatile farm sector. Fed's preferred productivity gauge.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Output, business, nonfarm
rics.meaning: Output, nonfarm business — total output.
rics.how_to_use: Numerator for nonfarm productivity. Output growth ≈ productivity growth + hours growth.

rics.description: Labour Productivity, Total-prelim
rics.meaning: Total productivity — preliminary.
rics.how_to_use: Watch revisions.

rics.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Reuters
rics.meaning: Series mislabeled in source as 'foreign exchange reserves' — actually nonfarm productivity/labor costs related.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-section / drill-down series; verify source before using.

rics.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Reuters
rics.meaning: Series mislabeled in source as 'foreign exchange reserves' — actually labor costs related.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-section / drill-down series; verify source before using.
